honest_take: ds4 already has a local kvdisk warm cache. When that cache is intact, ds4-native is unbeatable: the local round-trip is 36 ms; WombatKV's S3 GET overhead is pure cost. WombatKV's job is when the local cache is gone (process restart wiped it, machine swap, teammate inheriting state). This row is the floor of when WombatKV is the wrong answer.
Single prompt, no restart, engine is fully warm. WombatKV has nothing to restore. The prefetcher and chain-lookup cost a few percent. Honest baseline: WombatKV does not help warm engines.

5 users × 3 turns, no restart between users, warm decode. WombatKV is invoked but the engine's own RAM cache services everything. Bucket fills (69-176 keys) without intra-user TTFT improvement. Validates correctness across all 5 transport modes; not a speedup story.
Cross-host TCP over WiFi LAN. The KV state is ~23 MiB on the wire. Bandwidth-bound, not Wombat-bound. A wired LAN or RDMA fabric would help; the substrate has the hooks but the alpha doesn't.
Cross-host S3 (MinIO over LAN). 18× expansion vs loopback (108 ms → 1947 ms). Real production S3 will land between this 4.5× and the 73.1× loopback headline depending on latency.

Same workload (2048-token sweep), same Mac, two deployment shapes. Embedded mode wins because there's no IPC: 34.8×. Daemon-TCP through loopback adds framing and a context switch: 15.2×. Both wins; daemon mode pays an IPC tax in exchange for multi-engine sharing.

MinIO loopback GET latency is ~15 ms; real AWS S3 / R2 / GCS is 30-100 ms. The 73.1× canonical headline will compress on production endpoints. Until we have real cloud numbers, our 25-35× projection is the honest expectation.
